title: 15 countries ran unopposed for the UN Human Rights Council, but each still needed 97 votes
body: On 13 October 2026 the UN General Assembly [elected 15 members](https://press.un.org/en/2026/ga12795.doc.htm) of its 47-member Human Rights Council for 2027 to 2029. The seats are shared among five regional groups (13 for Africa, 13 for Asia-Pacific, 6 for Eastern Europe, 8 for Latin America and the Caribbean, 7 for Western Europe and others); a third come up each year, and no member may serve more than two terms in a row, so China, Côte d’Ivoire, Cuba, France and Malawi could not run again. This year every group put up exactly as many candidates as it had seats, but under [resolution 60/251](https://www2.ohchr.org/english/bodies/hrcouncil/docs/A.RES.60.251_En.pdf) each still needed votes from a majority of all 193 UN members, 97, in a secret ballot; all got between 160 and 177. In contested years the bar and the rivals both matter: [in 2023](https://news.un.org/en/story/2023/10/1142112) Russia got 83 votes and missed out, and Peru got 108 but came fourth for three seats. Suspension is counted differently, by two-thirds of the members voting yes or no: [in April 2022](https://news.un.org/en/story/2022/04/1115782) the Assembly suspended Russia by 93 votes to 24, with 58 abstentions.

slides.question: The UN has 193 member states. How many votes does a country need to win a seat on the UN Human Rights Council?
slides.explanation: 97, a majority of all 193 members, even with no rival. On 13 October 2026 all 15 unopposed candidates passed it, with 160 to 177 votes each.

slides.alt: Animation on night blue: the UN Human Rights Council's 47 seats as a ring coloured by region, 15 of them renewed. Columns of 15 candidates for 15 seats, bars of their votes past a gold line at 97, the contested 2023 races, and 193 dots for the 2022 vote to suspend Russia, 93 to 24.

slides.prompt: Set the votes for, against and abstaining. Find a vote that is enough to suspend a member but not enough to elect one.
slides.takeaway: A suspension counts only yes and no: 93 for and 24 against passes, as for Russia in 2022, though 93 is short of the 97 a country needs from all 193 members to join.

slides.heading: Human Rights Council, 2023: three countries for two Eastern European seats
slides.note: 97 votes needed; the top two won. UN News, 10 October 2023.

slides.heading: Two counts in the UN General Assembly

left.label: Joining the Council
left.text: Votes from 97 of the 193 UN members, by secret ballot, even with no rival.

right.label: Suspending a member
right.text: Two-thirds of the members voting yes or no. Abstentions don’t count.

slides.question: In April 2022, 93 UN members voted to suspend Russia from the Human Rights Council and 24 voted against. Why was 93 enough?
options: Only yes and no votes count
slides.explanation: Suspension needs two-thirds of the members voting yes or no. 93 of 117 is about 79%; the 58 abstentions were left out of the count.

source.label: UN press release GA/12795: General Assembly elects 15 members to Human Rights Council
